source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rural.evidence: Nippon India Mutual Fund's AUM from 'Beyond Top 30 cities' (B-30) stood at Rs 1.32 trillion, representing 19.8% of NIMF's AUM vs 18.6% industry average (proxy for rural/semi-urban penetration, not a revenue % per se).

inr_exposure.evidence: NAM-INDIA has overseas subsidiaries in Singapore (Nippon Life India Asset Management (Singapore) Pte Ltd, AUM USD 1.78bn offshore + USD 233mn advisory as of Mar 2025) and Mauritius, serving international investors; this international business is a small single-digit share of total AUM/revenue but exact % not disclosed in accessible sources.

rural.evidence: IHCL's midscale/regional brands (Ginger, Gateway, Tree of Life) are expanding into tier-2/tier-3 and regional/religious-tourism markets under its 'Accelerate 2030' capital-light growth strategy; no explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: UDAN scheme's third round added 106 new tourism air routes (53 operational by Jan 2025), and improved highway/airport infrastructure is cited by management and industry commentary as a demand driver; IHCL itself committed ₹7,500 crore capex over 5 years (internally funded) to capture this growth. No revenue % tied to govt capex disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL reported nil net debt and a strong gross cash position of INR 3,073 crore as of March 31, 2025, indicating low overall interest-rate sensitivity; floating-rate liability % not separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL earns foreign-currency revenue via international properties (St James' Court London, Taj Boston, The Pierre New York, Taj Cape Town); FY25 international occupancy improved ~440bps to 73%, though the UK business faced headwinds. Exact USD/GBP revenue % and hedging policy not found in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Management commentary describes a 'local for local' manufacturing commitment and notes that 'geopolitical uncertainties and their impact on supply chain remain a concern,' positioning Bosch India's localization as resilience; FY25 Mobility segment product sales grew 7.0% (domestic +6.2%) with 'export demand, particularly in off-highway components and software services,' also increasing. No explicit attribution of revenue growth to China+1 sourcing shifts was found — mentions exports/localization without an explicit diversification-from-China framing.

rural.evidence: FY25 Powertrain Solutions sales grew on tractor-segment strength (an agri/rural demand proxy), but no rural revenue % is disclosed for this B2B auto-components business.

inr_exposure.evidence: Bosch Ltd exports mobility components (partly to the Bosch Group in Europe) and FY25 revenue was reported in both INR (₹18,087 crore) and EUR (€1,985 million) by the German parent, implying meaningful EUR-denominated exposure, but no explicit export revenue % or hedging policy was found disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch is listed among approved beneficiaries of the 'Component Champion Incentive Scheme' under India's PLI Scheme for the Automobile and Auto Components industry (alongside Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Tata Autocomp, Motherson Sumi, Lucas-TVS, etc.), per India Briefing's compiled list of approvals. Revenue/incentive amount not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sun Pharma discloses strong US (31% of FY25 revenue) and Emerging Markets (18%) formulation growth across 80+ countries, but no company-specific China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative was found attributing this growth to diversification away from China. (Separately, India's government-run PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs is explicitly framed around reducing API import dependence on China, but this is a policy-level, not company-specific, narrative.)

inr_exposure.evidence: US formulations alone were 31% of FY25 revenue (~Rs 54,543 crore total revenue), Sun Pharma's single largest USD-denominated exposure; a portion of the 18% Emerging Markets and 14% RoW/API revenue is also foreign-currency. Exact aggregate USD revenue % and hedging/forward-contract policy not found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's pharma API/KSM PLI scheme's publicly named major beneficiaries (per Business Standard, citing govt data) are Dr Reddy's, Cipla, Glenmark, Biocon and Wockhardt; Sun Pharma was not identified as a named beneficiary in accessible sources, though its scheme eligibility/participation could not be fully ruled out without the primary annual report.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's API Plus/CDMO business (legacy API + Lupin Manufacturing Solutions) is described as offering 'global customers credible, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions as the world seeks secure and diversified API sources,' with alignment to 'global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs' and positioning to 'ensure secure global supply chains.' No explicit naming of China or quantified revenue attribution to diversification-driven order wins was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company discloses exposure primarily to USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR given operations across 100+ markets; deploys natural hedges and forex derivatives via treasury with a layered hedging approach. Exact hedge coverage ratio not disclosed in accessible sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: Lupin operates in 100+ markets and cites USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR as primary currency exposures; FY2025 US revenue of USD 925mn (~36% of total sales) is the largest single-currency exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin was named among 9 domestic companies (with Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Cadila/Zydus, Cipla, Glenmark, Intas, Torrent Pharma) approved under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Bulk Drugs/KSM/API), Group A category. Revenue/incentive amount specific to Lupin not disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source description of Alkem's raw-material supply chain: sourcing 'primarily from domestic Indian suppliers supplemented by imports from key global partners in the United States, Germany, and Spain, while maintaining low direct exposure to high-risk regions like China.' Separately, China (and Mexico) were cited as future international markets Alkem itself intends to expand INTO for its own products, not as a diversification-driven export tailwind. No revenue/order growth was attributed to a China+1 dynamic.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alkem does not appear among the named Group A beneficiaries of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Cadila, Cipla, Glenmark, Intas, Torrent, Lupin); no Alkem-specific PLI disclosure located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company describes strategic diversification 'across products, customers, and geographies' to mitigate dependency risk, and references satellite final-assembly facilities in the US, Mexico and China. Notably, Sona Comstar also entered a ~₹167 crore JV (60% stake) to manufacture driveline systems INSIDE China to access the local EV market — described by some commentators as 'China+1 in reverse' — which complicates a simple narrative of global OEMs shifting orders to Sona Comstar to de-risk from China. No AR text found explicitly attributing FY24-25 revenue/order growth to customers' China+1 diversification strategy; large EV order-book wins (e.g., ClearMotion, North American RV maker) were reported but mostly outside the FY24-25 reporting period.

crude_exposure.evidence: Steel, aluminum and plastics (partly crude-oil derived) are cited as primary raw material inputs for driveline/forging/motor manufacturing; no specific % of raw material cost tied to crude-linked commodities was found in accessible sources (direct PDF/notes access blocked by 403 errors).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is ~59% of FY25 total (North America 30%, Europe 24%, Asia-Pacific 5%), implying material USD and EUR exposure; specific hedging policy from Notes to Financial Statements could not be retrieved (all direct fetch attempts to sonacomstar.com AR PDFs returned HTTP 403 or unreadable binary).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first automotive component supplier to receive certification under India's Auto PLI (Production-Linked Incentive) scheme, for a hub-wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers; the company has filed 7 applications for different products under the scheme. Revenue contribution specifically attributable to PLI-linked sales was not quantified in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: CDMO/contract-manufacturing segment described as generating 'steady income from global clients, diversifying revenue streams,' serving multinational clients (J&J, P&G, Reckitt Benckiser, iNova) across 40+ countries including the US, UK, Australia, Brazil, Canada and South Africa; CDMO revenue grew ~18% YoY (₹129cr in Q4 FY25). International formulations business (Russia, South Africa focus) also grew. No explicit 'China+1' or China-specific supply-chain-diversification framing was found in accessible sources; classified moderate based on general export-momentum-plus-diversification language only.

inr_exposure.evidence: International + CDMO business (~42% of FY25 consolidated revenue of ~₹3,960cr; domestic ₹2,269cr, international ₹1,649cr) generates material foreign-currency revenue (USD/GBP via CDMO clients in US/UK/Australia/Canada, plus RUB exposure via Russia-focused international formulations); no specific USD % split or hedging policy was disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: J B Chemicals does not appear among the named Group A beneficiaries of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Cadila, Cipla, Glenmark, Intas, Torrent, Lupin); no company-specific PLI disclosure located in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix: India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, other markets 15% (45% export total). Currency exposure spans USD, EUR and BRL rather than USD alone; exact USD-denominated revenue share and hedging policy were not accessible in sources reviewed (primary AR PDF and Screener.in both returned HTTP 403).

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharma is listed among companies qualified under India's PLI scheme for the pharmaceutical sector (Dept. of Pharmaceuticals PLI for bulk drugs/formulations); exact revenue percentage attributable to PLI-linked production not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 revenue commentary and industry analysis tied to Divi's results state that major global drugmakers are diversifying supply chains to limit reliance on China, benefiting Divi's and Indian API peers. Divi's pursued backward integration into fermentation-based APIs/KSMs (e.g., Gabapentin, Naproxen, Valsartan, Levetiracetam) explicitly to reduce import dependency on China, with Kakinada Phase I operational to support this. New long-term Custom Synthesis contracts (revenue visibility from FY27) were attributed by management/analysts to this global supply-chain diversification trend, and the PLI scheme's stated goal of cutting API/KSM import dependence on China by 25-30% over 4-5 years directly supports Divi's positioning.

rural.evidence: Not applicable - Divi's is a B2B API/CDMO exporter serving global pharma innovators and generics majors, not a rural-facing consumer business.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Divi's is reported as effectively debt-free (very low debt-to-equity), implying minimal floating-rate liability exposure; exact floating-vs-fixed borrowing split not accessible in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Earnings-call commentary in prior years noted sharp increases in solvent and catalyst-metal costs (petrochemical-linked inputs), with more recent commentary noting stabilization aided by diversified sourcing and buffer stock; no explicit percentage of raw materials tied to crude/petrochemical inputs was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue by geography: Europe ~56%, North America ~16%, India ~12%, Asia ~11%, Rest of World ~4% (88% total export). Revenue is largely foreign-currency denominated but the primary AR (financial risk management notes) was not accessible (403 errors on screener.in, divislabs.com and IR PDF links), so exact USD share and hedging policy could not be confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's has pursued PLI-aligned capacity expansion in fermentation-based APIs and KSMs previously uneconomical domestically due to Chinese pricing, via backward integration (Kakinada facility). Exact revenue percentage attributable to PLI-linked products not disclosed in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Company describes a pan-India network of 60,000+ retail outlets with explicit emphasis on semi-urban/rural penetration for value/mass 'Regular & Economy' brands (8PM Whisky, Contessa Rum), which constitute the majority of IMFL volume (Prestige & Above rose to 43.4% of IMFL volume in FY25 from 36.5% prior year, implying ~56% still Regular/mass, which typically over-indexes rural/semi-urban demand). No explicit rural revenue percentage is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt was reduced meaningfully in FY25 versus FY24, indicating low and declining leverage overall; exact floating-vs-fixed rate split not accessible in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Crude oil is not a direct raw-material driver; key inputs are grain, ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass bottles. Commentary notes grain/ENA/glass price volatility pressured gross margins in FY24, with packaging costs up materially, and guidance for grain/ENA turning stable-to-favourable into FY25/26. No crude/fuel-linked cost quantification found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports represent roughly 9-10% of revenue (multi-currency, sold across 85-100+ countries plus duty-free/CSD channels), implying limited overall FX exposure. No explicit USD revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure was located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcobev is not a PLI-covered sector; no PLI participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary around FY25 results frames Navin Fluorine as a beneficiary of global customers' preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment, supporting its export-led HPP (specialty refrigerants) and CDMO agrochemical/pharma-intermediate business; the company commercialized its R32 refrigerant project (Mar-2025) and signed a Chemours Opteon (immersion-cooling fluid) manufacturing agreement, both framed by analysts as diversification-driven wins. Customer concentration in exports (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva, Fermion) rose to ~80% in H1FY26 from ~63% in FY24. Direct AR MD&A text explicitly using 'China+1' framing with revenue attribution could not be confirmed since the primary AR PDF (nfil.in) returned HTTP 403.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are fluorspar and hydrofluoric acid (HF), not crude oil directly, though HF and associated solvents have petrochemical-linked cost components. The company commissioned a new AHF (anhydrous HF) plant at Dahej for backward integration, reducing external fluorspar/HF purchase dependency. No raw-material cost percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~65% of FY25 revenue (down slightly from ~66% in FY24; Q4FY25 export share was higher at ~77%), largely USD-denominated for the specialty chemicals/HPP/CDMO export business. Exact USD revenue percentage and hedging policy were not accessible (primary AR PDF blocked).

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI scheme for chemicals/petrochemicals has been discussed by the Indian government but no confirmation was found that Navin Fluorine is a designated PLI beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: Zydus MD Sharvil Patel has publicly stated that roughly 60% of medicines consumed in the US are manufactured in India, framing India (and Zydus) as a beneficiary of supply-chain diversification away from China; broader Indian pharma industry commentary links the government's API PLI scheme to reducing China import dependence. This is industry/management commentary picked up in press coverage, not confirmed as explicit language with revenue attribution inside the FY24-25 Annual Report MD&A itself (primary AR PDF could not be fetched — zyduslife.com, NSE archive, and Screener.in all returned HTTP 403).

crude_exposure.evidence: Zydus API manufacturing uses petrochemical-derived raw materials. Zydus MD Sharvil Patel publicly flagged (Mar 2026 press commentary) that an oil/gas price crisis could pressure pharma/API input costs industry-wide with a 2-3 month lag, while regulated medicine pricing limits cost pass-through. No specific raw-material-cost percentage tied to crude was disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment revenue mix (per Q4FY25 results commentary) was approximately: India Formulations 21.8%, US Formulations 35.2%, International Markets Formulations 13.8%, Consumer Wellness 9.6%, Medtech 10.9%, Others 8.7% — implying meaningful foreign-currency (largely USD) revenue exposure via the US and International Markets segments, but a precise consolidated USD-revenue percentage and hedging/forward-contract policy could not be confirmed from the Annual Report notes (unreachable).

pli_scheme.evidence: India operates a PLI scheme for KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs aimed at import substitution from China, and Zydus has multiple API manufacturing facilities (e.g., Ambernath) that could plausibly qualify, but no source found explicitly confirms Zydus Lifesciences as an approved PLI scheme beneficiary or discloses PLI-linked revenue.

rural.evidence: Phoenix Mills operates urban malls, retail (Phoenix MarketCity, Palladium), and commercial/office properties concentrated in metro and tier-1 Indian cities (Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Chennai, etc.); no rural revenue disclosure exists as this is a domestic urban consumption/retail-rental REIT-like business, not a rural-facing model.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company commentary (Q3/Q4 FY25 earnings materials, via secondary sources) indicates group gross debt of roughly INR 4,400-4,600 crore with average cost of debt declining from ~9.2% to ~8.5% during FY25 and Net Debt/EBITDA around 1.2x. As a leveraged real estate/mall operator this points to plausible floating-rate exposure, but the specific fixed-vs-floating borrowing mix and the interest-rate-risk note that would confirm it could not be retrieved — thephoenixmills.com and Screener.in both returned HTTP 403 on all annual report/document fetch attempts.

inr_exposure.evidence: No mention of foreign-currency-denominated debt (e.g., ECBs) or USD revenue exposure found in accessible secondary sources; company appears to be a domestic INR-denominated business, but the borrowings note that would confirm this (foreign currency loans, if any) could not be accessed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IKS was debt-free prior to FY24. It raised roughly INR 11,934 million of borrowings (INR 8,123mn long-term + INR 3,811mn current) in FY24 to fund the Aquity Solutions acquisition (total consideration ~INR 16,740mn). Net debt was reduced from ~INR 8,500mn (FY24) to ~INR 5,030mn by 9M FY25, including refinancing a USD term loan down from ~$146mn to ~$50mn; the company has stated an ambition to be debt-free by FY27, though it subsequently arranged large new USD facilities (~$635-670mn) for the FY26 TruBridge acquisition. USD-denominated term loans of this type are typically SOFR-linked floating-rate facilities, implying meaningful floating-rate exposure, but the exact floating-vs-fixed split was not disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: IKS Health derives approximately 96% of consolidated revenue from US clients (healthcare BPO/RCM services), with the remainder from other geographies (Canada, Australia). Delivery is staffed substantially out of India, creating a natural USD-revenue/INR-cost mismatch. A subsequent-period (Q3 FY26) results update referenced a ~INR 90 million hedging loss recognized within the revenue line, confirming the company does use forex hedging instruments, but the specific hedging policy, hedge ratio, or % of revenue hedged was not disclosed in accessible sources (annual report notes/MD&A were unreachable — ikshealth.com and Screener.in both returned HTTP 403).

rural.evidence: Nykaa's B2B distribution arm 'Superstore by Nykaa' generated ~89% of its FY25 GMV (₹941 crore) from Tier II and smaller markets, serving ~280,000 transacting retailers across ~1,100 cities — but this figure is specific to the Superstore segment, not overall company revenue. Broader FY25 commentary confirms an active omnichannel physical-store expansion (~250 stores) into smaller cities as part of Nykaa's growth strategy, and management has cited higher average order values from Tier 2/3 customers, but a company-wide Tier 2/3/rural revenue percentage was not found in accessible sources (nykaa.com, Screener.in, and Scribd all returned HTTP 403 on document fetch attempts).

inr_exposure.evidence: Nykaa's Luxe format retails international beauty brands (e.g., Huda Beauty, MAC, Dior, Givenchy) sourced from abroad, implying some import/USD-denominated procurement exposure, but no quantified USD revenue/cost percentage or hedging policy disclosure was found in accessible sources. Separately, international revenue (Middle East operations via UAE/Qatar/Oman subsidiaries and a UK partnership for Kay Beauty) is reported as below 1% of overall company revenue, indicating the business is overwhelmingly domestic-India-facing.

rural.evidence: Secondary-source city-tier sales mix cited for FY2024-25: Metro 23%, Town Class 1 27%, Town Class 2-6 28%, Rural 22% of domestic sales. Could not be verified against the primary Annual Report (WebFetch on the AR PDF and Screener page returned HTTP 403); rural franchise is nonetheless a long-standing core part of Mankind's mass-market brand strategy (Manforce, Prega News, Unwanted-72).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is a small and growing share of total revenue (roughly 9-14% across recent quarters/years, boosted by the BSV international acquisition), implying limited but rising foreign-currency exposure. No explicit hedging policy disclosure located.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed disclosure of Mankind Pharma as a registered beneficiary under either the Pharmaceuticals PLI (formulations) or Bulk Drugs/API PLI schemes was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Broader industry commentary links India's manufacturing FDI growth (+18% YoY to ~USD 19.04bn in FY2024-25) to a China+1 diversification wave, but no company-specific statement attributing Siemens India's revenue/order growth to China+1 dynamics was located. Separately, Siemens' record ₹3bn/1,200-unit locomotive order for Indian Railways is ~90% locally sourced, reflecting Make-in-India import substitution rather than an export/diversification narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: Government/public-sector demand is a material driver: FY2024 New Orders were ₹235,641 million (down from ₹463,829 million in FY2023, which included a large 9,000HP electric locomotive order from Indian Railways); Order Backlog stood at ₹482,639 million as of Sept 30, 2024. Siemens Mobility separately won a record ~€3 billion / 1,200-locomotive order from Indian Railways (largest in Siemens Mobility's history), with locomotives assembled at the Indian Railways factory in Dahod, Gujarat. No exact % of revenue tied to government/rail contracts was disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: A PLI scheme for railway train-component manufacturers has been proposed/discussed by the Indian government (₹1,000-1,500 crore outlay) to cut import dependence on Vande Bharat/LHB components, but no confirmation that Siemens is a registered beneficiary was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit 'China+1' or supply-chain-diversification-from-China framing found. FY25 international revenue (~57% of consolidated revenue, up on 9.5% volume growth) is discussed in terms of global reach (75+ countries) and wire-rope exports (~40% of wire-rope production exported to 100+ countries), but not attributed to China+1 dynamics. Usha Martin itself operates a China subsidiary (Usha Martin China Co. Ltd, Shanghai), which cuts against a pure alternative-to-China positioning.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Historically (FY2019-20 AR) floating-rate liabilities were ~64% of total financial liabilities (₹690.97 cr of ₹1,077.46 cr), with 1% rate sensitivity of ~₹6.44 cr to PBT. Since divesting its integrated steel/coking-coal business (FY19-21) the company has deleveraged sharply — net debt was only ₹63 cr in FY25, moving to a net cash position of ₹332 cr in FY26 — so the current floating-rate mix is likely far smaller, but an updated % was not found in accessible sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Core raw material is steel wire rod, largely externally sourced after Usha Martin divested its integrated/coking-coal-linked steelmaking business (FY19-21); no crude-oil-linked raw material exposure identified. Cost-as-%-of-revenue breakdown not accessible.

inr_exposure.evidence: International markets account for ~57% of FY25 consolidated revenue, spanning Europe (~26%), Asia Pacific (~14%), Middle East & Africa (~9%) and Americas (~8%), implying material foreign-currency revenue exposure. Explicit USD-denominated share and hedging policy not found (primary AR PDF and Screener page returned HTTP 403 on all fetch attempts).

china_plus_one.evidence: No literal 'China+1' term found, but a clear supply-chain diversification/resilience narrative is documented: CCL's dual manufacturing base in India and Vietnam functions as a tariff hedge — when the US imposed higher tariffs on Indian-origin coffee, CCL shifted volumes through its Vietnam facility (which sits in the world's largest Robusta-growing region, enjoys ASEAN duty-free access and tax-exempt status) to sustain export competitiveness. CCL is expanding Vietnam capacity (+13,500 tpa, targeting 27,000 tpa, total capacity path to ~52,000 tpa). Separately, secondary commentary notes European buyers facing higher costs are outsourcing coffee production to Brazil, India and Vietnam, a tailwind for CCL — but this is not phrased as a China-specific diversification story since China is not a coffee-export competitor in this space.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Not confirmed from the primary Annual Report (all direct PDF/IR fetches returned HTTP 403). Secondary analyst commentary describes a partial natural hedge: a large share of raw material cost (green coffee) is also USD-denominated, offsetting USD export revenue, supplemented by hedging instruments and customer pricing clauses, though risk is not fully eliminated.
inr_exposure.evidence: CCL exports to ~90 countries and is India's largest instant-coffee exporter / the world's largest private-label instant coffee manufacturer; largest disclosed markets are CIS (~20-25%), Europe (~12-15%) and North America (~12-14%) per tertiary analyst sources (not the primary AR), implying large multi-currency export exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Unconfirmed. One analyst blog loosely references 'PLI scheme continuity' benefiting the instant-coffee sector, but the official PLI Scheme for Food Processing Industries (PLISFPI) product list (RTC/RTE foods incl. millet products, processed fruits & vegetables, marine products, mozzarella cheese) does not explicitly include instant coffee, and no primary-source confirmation of CCL as a registered beneficiary was found.
